Lifetimes are how the Rust compiler reasons about how long references stay valid. Most of the time they are elided, but a function that returns a reference derived from two inputs needs an explicit lifetime parameter so the compiler knows which input the result borrows from. A struct that holds a reference must carry a lifetime too. The error "borrowed value does not live long enough" means a reference would outlive the data it points to. Lifetimes are the compile-time half of [[Rust ownership]].
